name: Rabbit White Korma with Cashew Cream
description: French rabbit (lapin) slow-braised in a silky Pakistani-style white korma of cashew paste, heavy cream and white pepper. A halal fusion recipe combining Lahori korma technique with French braising discipline.
keywords: rabbit white korma, lapin korma, white korma recipe, halal rabbit curry, cashew korma, French-Pakistani fusion
recipeIngredient: 1 whole rabbit, about 1.3 kg (2 lb 14 oz), jointed into 8 pieces
120 g raw cashews, soaked 30 min in hot water
2 medium white onions, about 350 g total, thinly sliced
1 tsp ground white pepper (for korma base)
½ tsp ground ginger (for korma base)
½ tsp fine sea salt (for korma base)
200 ml warm water or unsalted chicken stock
Small pinch of saffron, steeped in 2 tbsp warm milk
Flaked almonds, lightly toasted, to serve

recipeInstructions.name: Marinate the rabbit
recipeInstructions.text: Mix the yoghurt, salt, white pepper, ground ginger and ground coriander in a large bowl. Add the rabbit pieces and turn to coat thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 2 hours, or overnight. Bring to room temperature 30 minutes before cooking.

recipeInstructions.name: Make the cashew paste
recipeInstructions.text: Drain the soaked cashews, transfer to a blender with 80 ml warm water, and blend on high for 2 minutes until completely smooth. Add the rose water, pulse once to combine, and set aside.

recipeInstructions.name: Fry the whole spices
recipeInstructions.text: In a wide, heavy-bottomed pot, heat the oil and butter together over medium heat until the butter foam subsides. Add the cardamom, cloves, bay leaf, mace and cassia. Stir for 60 to 90 seconds until the cloves swell and the cassia uncurls.

recipeInstructions.name: Cook the onions
recipeInstructions.text: Add the sliced onions and a pinch of salt. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring every few minutes, for 22 to 28 minutes, until the onions are deep mahogany.

recipeInstructions.name: Add ground spices and bhunno
recipeInstructions.text: Add the ground white pepper and ground ginger. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until the oil separates at the edges of the pan.

recipeInstructions.name: Add cashew paste and bhunno again
recipeInstructions.text: Pour in the cashew paste. Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, for 5 to 7 minutes until the paste tightens, sticks slightly at the edges, and the oil separates again.

recipeInstructions.name: Brown the rabbit
recipeInstructions.text: Push the masala to the sides of the pot. Increase heat to medium-high. Add the marinated rabbit pieces and brown lightly on both sides, 2 to 3 minutes per side.

recipeInstructions.name: Braise
recipeInstructions.text: Add the warm water or stock, stir once to integrate, and bring to a gentle simmer. Cover tightly, reduce to low, and cook for 55 to 65 minutes, turning the rabbit pieces once at the halfway point.

recipeInstructions.name: Finish the sauce
recipeInstructions.text: Uncover the pot and raise heat to medium. Reduce any excess liquid for 5 minutes if needed. Add the cream, stir gently, and cook for 3 minutes. Add the kewra water and saffron-steeped milk. Taste and adjust salt.

recipeInstructions.name: Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Transfer to a warmed serving dish. Scatter toasted flaked almonds and torn mint over the top. Serve with layered paratha, plain basmati, or a French baguette.
